label: clean
rationale: 0/804 graded scenarios failed, so there is no failure to attribute and `clean` is the only label the outcome permits. Recorded rather than left absent so a reader can tell a trial that was read from one that was not. The pass carries no information about the mechanism: challenge/README.md line 19 describes challenge/starter/subject.mjs as "a stub with the required export shape" and the file self-labels "Starter stub - replace me" (line 38), but I re-graded the shipped starter against all 804 hidden scenarios and it fails 0. The visible package contained a complete passing solution. `package-leak` is the substantive finding, but it attributes a failure and this trial failed nothing, so the format refuses that label (ROOTCAUSE_LABEL_CONTRADICTS_OUTCOME) and the leak is recorded here instead. The family is self-consistent -- its reference subject scores 0/804 -- so this is a packaging defect rather than a verifier fault. Note for anyone re-measuring this family: its 804 scenarios share only 48 distinct idempotency keys, so a re-grade that reuses one subject module instance across scenarios will produce large spurious duplicate-spend failures; each scenario must get a fresh module, as the recorded subprocess host did.
